questions.question_text:
The grouped frequency table shows weekly hours of music practice.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Hours}&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0-4&5\\ 5-9&14\\ 10-14&23\\ 15-19&8\end{array}$
State the modal class.

options.why: Reported the maximum frequency rather than the class interval.
Reported the class centre of the modal class instead of the class interval.
Selected the second class rather than the class with the highest frequency.

questions.question_text:
The table shows the masses (in kg) of $50$ dogs at a shelter.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Mass (kg)}&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0 < m \le 10&6\\ 10 < m \le 20&18\\ 20 < m \le 30&16\\ 30 < m \le 40&10\end{array}$
What is the median class?

options.why: Identified the modal class (highest frequency of 18) instead of the median class.
Reported the class centre of the second class instead of the median class interval.
Reported the median position rather than the class interval.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Position} = \frac{50 + 1}{2}$
$= 25.5$
$\text{Cumulative frequencies: } 6, 24, 40, 50$
The $25.5\text{th}$ score lies in the third class.
$\text{Median class} = 20 < m \le 30$

questions.question_text:
A grouped frequency table is shown below.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Class interval}&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 21-30&6\\ 31-40&11\\ 41-50&3\end{array}$
Calculate the estimated mean of this distribution.

options.why: Averaged the class centres (25.5 + 35.5 + 45.5)/3 without weighting by frequencies.
Calculated the sum of cc * f (680) but forgot to divide by the total frequency (20).
Used the upper class boundaries (30, 40, 50) instead of the class centres.

questions.question_text:
The table shows the call durations (in minutes) for $40$ support calls.
$\begin{array}{c|c}\text{Duration (min)}&\text{Frequency }(f)\\ \hline 0 < t \le 4&10\\ 4 < t \le 8&18\\ 8 < t \le 12&12\end{array}$
Find the estimated mean call duration.

options.why: Took the midpoint of the middle class instead of computing the weighted mean.
Calculated sum of cc * f without dividing by the total frequency of 40.
Used the upper class boundaries instead of the class centres.
Confused the median cumulative frequency position (40) with the median score.
Read off the upper boundary of the median class instead of reading from 50% cumulative frequency.
Reported the total number of students surveyed rather than the median score.

questions.question_text: A table of ages has classes $0-19, 20-39, 40-59,$ and $60+$. Why is it impossible to estimate the mean from this grouped frequency table?

options.text: The open-ended class $60+$ has no upper limit, so its class centre cannot be calculated.
The class intervals are too wide to allow calculating a mean.
options.why: Class interval width does not prevent calculating an estimated mean.

options.text: A grouped frequency table can only be used to find the median, never the mean.
options.why: Grouped frequency tables can be used to estimate the mean if all class centres exist.

options.text: The data values in the $60+$ class must all be outliers.
options.why: Values in open-ended classes are not necessarily outliers.

questions.solution_text:
To estimate the mean, every class must have a defined class centre $cc = \frac{\text{lower} + \text{upper}}{2}$.
The open-ended class $60+$ has no upper boundary, so its class centre is undefined.

questions.question_text: A grouped frequency distribution of $20$ items across classes $0-9$ ($cc = 4.5, f = 6$), $10-19$ ($cc = 14.5, f = k$), and $20-29$ ($cc = 24.5, f = 4$) has an estimated mean of $13.5$. What is the value of $k$?

options.why: Subtracted incorrectly from the total frequency (20 - 6 - 4 = 10, not 8).
Averaged the adjacent frequencies (6 + 4)/2 + 7 instead of solving the equation.
Confused the class centre with the missing frequency.
Estimated the median as the midpoint of the entire wage range (200 to 1000).
Read off the wage at 150 cumulative frequency instead of at 50% (100).
Confused the cumulative frequency position of 100 with a dollar value.

questions.solution_text:
$\text{Median position} = 50\% \text{ of } 200$
$= 100$
At cumulative frequency $100$, the ogive gives a wage of $\$600$.
$\text{Estimated median} = \$600$
